gaps.quote: Replacing the operands of a bilinear contraction $\mathcal B$
gaps.note: The page never says what a contraction is (a bilinear map with ||B(x,y)|| <= ||x|| ||y|| in the sup norm). The displayed bound needs exactly this property, so the reader cannot check it from the identity alone.

gaps.quote: for unit phase $e,$ approximation $\widetilde e,$ disk operand $x.$
gaps.note: Missing hypothesis: the paper (lines 4568-4576) requires the approximation to be a disk-grid number with |e~ - e| < 2h_p (so |e~| <= 1). Without that the bounds 4h_p and ||Q_p(e~x)|| <= ||x|| do not follow.

gaps.note: The page does not say why the transform errors are multiplied by M (the normalized result is rescaled by an exact multiplication by M, paper lines 4582-4592), nor what the ring convolution is.

gaps.quote: The source transform (error $2dp^2+8TL$ before scaling, then multiplied by $2^\gamma$)
gaps.note: The source transform, its expansion and compression stages, and where 2dp^2+8TL comes from (paper 4641-4650) are neither explained nor linked; the reader must take the figure on trust.

gaps.quote: The opposite transform gives error less than $(3E_s+2)h_p$
gaps.note: The page gives no derivation: it is E_s (computed opposite transform vs exact G applied to z) plus (2E_s+2) (G is a contraction applied to z - U.V_1), and it needs ||z|| < .5 so the computed transform is defined (paper 4695-4704).

An identity about the transforms that the page never states or justifies; it is the chirp-permutation lemma in the paper (4689-4694). The reader cannot see why three transforms of the convolution give (u*v)/S^2.
The page never says the digit arrays u,v are scaled (each by 2^-(b+2), giving norm < 1/4), so the factor 2^{2b+4} and the norm bounds needed to stay in the disk are unexplained.
The page never relates T, S, L to b, so the reader cannot check T < 2^b and L < b. Both hold only eventually for large n (paper 4722).

Inconsistent arithmetic: with p=6b and scaling spending 3b+4 bits, 6b-(3b+4)=3b-4 bits remain, not 4b. The paper has no such statement (the scaling widths are at lines 4737-4743), so the '(cited)' attribution is also unsupported.

gaps.quote: Dividing by $Q_0$ and $q\le n\le Q_0$ finish the step.
gaps.note: The page never says why n <= 2^b (b is only called the bits per digit); this comes from the parameter choice (paper 4193). Without it q(Q_0-1) < Q_0^2 does not follow.

False: from c_j+k_j=d_j+Q_0k_{j+1} (paper 4785) one gets c_j = d_j+Q_0k_{j+1}-k_j, so c_jQ_0^j=(d_j+Q_0k_{j+1}-k_j)Q_0^j. The -k_jQ_0^j term is what cancels the old k_jQ_0^j on the right side; as written the invariant would not carry from j to j+1.
